label: Basic Properties of Optimal Transport
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 43 through 50 and lays the foundations: the Kantorovich problem is a linear program over the convex set of couplings with fixed marginals. We motivate why an optimal coupling exists at all, and preview the structural signature of optimality, cyclical monotonicity, that organizes the rest of the book.

label: The Kantorovich Problem
notes: Recall the relaxed problem: minimize the integral of the cost against a coupling whose marginals are the prescribed measures mu and nu. The admissible set is never empty because the product measure always qualifies. We fix vocabulary, the transport cost functional and the optimal total cost, before studying when a minimizer is attained.

label: Standing Hypotheses
notes: The existence theorem rests on two mild hypotheses. The cost function is lower semicontinuous and bounded below, typically by zero on a Polish space. These are weak enough to cover squared distance and most natural costs, yet strong enough to make the cost functional behave well under weak limits of couplings.

label: The Set of Couplings is Convex
notes: The set of couplings with fixed marginals is convex: any mixture of two couplings is again a coupling, since the marginal constraints are linear. The cost functional is linear in the plan. So Kantorovich is an infinite-dimensional linear program, and we expect minima at extreme points of the admissible set.

label: Tightness and Prokhorov
notes: Each marginal is tight, so given epsilon we find compacts capturing mass in each factor. The product compact then captures the joint mass uniformly over all couplings. By Prokhorov, the family of couplings is precompact for weak convergence, and a minimizing sequence has a weakly convergent subsequence.

label: Lower Semicontinuity of the Cost
notes: Weak convergence alone does not preserve integrals, but lower semicontinuity of the cost gives the one-sided inequality we need. The total cost is weakly lower semicontinuous in the plan, so the limit of a minimizing sequence does no worse than the infimum. Combined with compactness this delivers a minimizer.

label: Existence of an Optimal Coupling
notes: Assemble the pieces by the direct method of the calculus of variations. The admissible set is weakly compact by Prokhorov, the cost is weakly lower semicontinuous, so the infimum is attained. Under a lower semicontinuous cost bounded below on Polish spaces, an optimal coupling always exists, with no convexity of the cost required.

label: Optimal Cost as a Function of Marginals
notes: Fixing the cost, the optimal total cost becomes a function of the pair of marginals. It inherits convexity from the linear structure and is itself lower semicontinuous: if the marginals converge weakly, the optimal cost does not jump up. This stability is what lets us later define Wasserstein distances and study their topology.

label: The Restriction Property
notes: Restriction is the chapter's most useful lemma. If a plan is optimal and we restrict it to a measurable subset of the product, then after renormalizing, the restriction is optimal for its own marginals. A cheaper sub-plan could be pasted back to beat the original, contradicting global optimality. Optimality is hereditary.

label: Cyclical Monotonicity Appears
notes: Restriction localizes optimality down to finite subsets of the support, and there it forces a combinatorial condition: no finite cyclic reshuffle of assigned pairs can lower the total cost. This is c-cyclical monotonicity, the structural signature of an optimal support, and the bridge to Kantorovich duality in the next chapter.

label: Polish Space Technicalities
notes: The measurability scaffolding matters. Working on Polish spaces keeps measures Radon and inner regular, lets us disintegrate plans, and ensures the restriction and gluing operations are well defined. These technical hypotheses are not decoration; they are exactly what makes tightness, Prokhorov, and the direct method legitimately applicable.

label: Summary and Outlook
notes: We proved existence from compactness and lower semicontinuity, saw the optimal cost is convex and stable in the marginals, established the restriction property, and met c-cyclical monotonicity. Next chapter turns this structural signature into Kantorovich duality, recovering optimal plans from a pair of dual potentials and the geometry of the support.
